thread:
anya: quick q — noticed clients seeing different headers on 429s from /v1/chat vs /v1/embedding, is that intentional?
devon: hmm, not intentionally. what differences are you seeing?
anya: /v1/chat returns Retry-After + X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining; /v1/embedding returns X-RateLimit-Remaining and no bucket id. SDKs expect a bucket id to decide per-route fallback.
maria: that sounds like a bug — embeddings used an older middleware path that didn't attach the new quota headers.
devon: thanks. for clarity, our desired contract is: always include Retry-After when we send 429 (seconds), and include these headers when applicable:
  X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: <int>
  X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket: <string>  # e.g. "acct:12345:route:embedding:short"
  X-Redwood-Quota-Reset: <unix_ts_seconds>
  X-Redwood-Quota-Type: "route"|"account"|"burst"
sdk-eng: client logic we ship today looks for Retry-After and then falls back to per-route queue if bucket id matches. If bucket id missing, it treats as account-level and backs off globally.
anya: ok — so embeddings should start emitting X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket. Is that safe for backcompat? older clients already check X-RateLimit-Remaining.
devon: we need to keep X-RateLimit-Remaining for older SDKs, yes. The new headers are additive.
maria: timeline-wise I can patch the embeddings middleware to attach quota headers by EOD tomorrow. small risk is we might have slight header format differences; i'll add tests.
anya: do we need a rollout plan? some customers prefer no new headers for compliance reasons.
devon: additive headers are low-risk. still let's gate behind a canary in prod: 5% of embedding traffic with the new header for 24h, monitor errors & SDK telemetry.
sre-bot: deploy scheduled: embedding-mw/patch-attach-quota-headers -> canary (5%) at 2026-03-18T15:00Z
sdk-eng: heads-up: we'll add a minor SDK change to prefer X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket if present, but keep fallback to X-RateLimit-Remaining. will ship a patch that tolerates missing bucket ids.
anya: also flag: how do we annotate soft-429s vs hard? i.e., when we want clients to retry quickly vs hard backoff.
devon: good call. we'll encode that in X-Redwood-Quota-Type: "burst" for soft grace, and "route" or "account" for hard limits. also still set Retry-After to seconds for client timers.
maria: tests: add unit that asserts headers present for embedding route when quota exceeded; add integration sim that ensures SDK falls back correctly.
anya: perfect. can you post the PR link here when ready? i'll ping product to confirm no compliance blockers.
maria: will do, PR up in ~3h -> https://git.redwood/emb/mw/attach-quota-headers (draft)
devon: thanks team. after canary and SDK patch we'll flip to 100% and update docs: docs/api/rate-limits.md with examples.
anya: awesome :thumbsup!
sre-bot: canary started: embedding-mw v2.3.1 -> 5% traffic
sdk-eng: noted. we'll watch telemetry and be ready to roll client patch if anything weird.
anya: if anything weird pops, @devon or @maria please @mention in #incidents.
anya: thanks all, closing this async thread.
